extracted.intended_audience: researchers, systematic reviewers, and policy-makers interested in publication bias and health technology assessment
extracted.subtask_description: A systematic review / meta-analysis examining publication bias (rate of publication of positive versus non-positive results) across cohort and abstract cohort studies in health research, reporting pooled effect sizes and heterogeneity and comparing sampling frames.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report pooled effect size with 95% CI
rubrics_metrics.description: Pooled odds ratio (OR) and 95% confidence interval reported for combined studies (example in text: pooled OR = 2.93 (2.31 to 3.71)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the combined effect estimate (e.g., pooled OR) with its 95% confidence interval when synthesising results across studies; give numerical example as shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report heterogeneity statistics (I2) and p-value
rubrics_metrics.description: Heterogeneity reported using I2 and associated p-value (example in text: heterogeneity: I2 = 17%, p = 0.27).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include measures of between-study heterogeneity (I2) and the statistical test p-value when presenting meta-analysis results to inform interpretation of pooled estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct sensitivity/exclusion analyses for influential studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform analyses after excluding particular studies to assess robustness (example: 'After excluding Misakian and Bero (1998)30 from inception cohort studies, pooled OR = 2.93 (2.31 to 3.71)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run sensitivity analyses that exclude potentially influential or outlying studies and report how pooled estimates change, explicitly naming excluded studies and resulting effect estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be inclusive of study types and compare sampling frames
rubrics_metrics.description: Include diverse types of studies and enable explicit comparisons across fundamentally different sampling frames (the review states it is more inclusive and enables explicit comparison of results from cohort studies with different sampling frames).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the review to capture various study designs/sampling frames and present comparative analyses to explore how sampling strategy affects observed publication bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess publication bias across stages of the research dissemination process
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine where in the dissemination process selection for publication occurs (finding: 'publication bias occurs mainly before the presentation of findings at conferences and before the submission of manuscript to journals').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyse publication bias at multiple stages (pre-presentation, post-presentation/pre-submission, post-submission) rather than treating publication as a single endpoint; report stage-specific pooled associations where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report numbers and characteristics of included study cohorts
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide counts and descriptions of included cohorts (example: 'was examined in 16 of 79 abstract cohort studies' and 'According to these 16 abstract cohort studies...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the number of studies/cohorts contributing to each analysis and describe their characteristics so readers can judge evidence breadth and applicability.
